question: Can a finite closed directional packet produce steady friction, and what material contract is required?
assumptions: fixed real contact mask and closed finite full 0/1/2 generator; y(0)=z(0)=0
native averaging s=t/tau only for constant positive tau
reciprocal local material quadratic energy with stable K and nonnegative Rayleigh loss D
cross-Hessian addition residual formula holds common K,D
physical_mapping: packet-to-dimensional C_add, physical clock, contact, loss and force readout OPEN
target_exposure: paired 21.8/38.2 degree signal and weak load trend known before analysis; no coefficient fit
baseline: full conventional 2D PES/contact and complex loss, calibrated without held-out signed force/load
result: EXACT closed finite fixed-mask packet J and harmonic P are odd finite trigonometric sums with zero Cesaro mean. CONDITIONAL reciprocal material damping Gamma=C K^-1 D K^-1 C^T, derivative and potentially negative baseline-subtracted residual. No physical graphite coefficient.
next_discriminant: Obtain independently registered packet-to-C_add map, material loss and pressure derivatives, then forecast signed held-out angle/speed/load forces.
